content.title: About
content.content: The French roll (sometimes called Vienna roll) is a light, airy bread roll made from wheat flour, yeast, milk, butter, and a small amount of sugar. The dough is allowed to rise, creating a characteristic porous crumb, then shaped into small round buns and baked to a golden crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally the French roll is baked in French and Austrian bakeries, where it is served at breakfast or as a snack.
The name "Vienna" arose from the roll's popularity in Viennese cafés in the 19th century.
The dough is often proofed for more than 12 hours, which develops complex aromatic compounds.
In some regions the rolls are sprinkled with coarse sea salt or poppy seeds for extra flavor and texture.
French rolls are frequently used as a base for ham, cheese, and fresh‑vegetable sandwiches.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The roll provides a quick source of energy thanks to easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: The dough supplies B1, B2 and niacin, which support metabolism.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Flour and milk deliver calcium, iron and magnesium.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with baguettes or croissants, the roll contains less saturated fat.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Its soft, porous texture makes it gentle on the digestive system, especially for children and seniors.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The roll contains wheat flour and is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because of rapid carbohydrate absorption, the roll can raise blood sugar levels, which is important for diabetics to consider.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions are salted; those monitoring sodium intake should choose an unsalted option.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the roll fresh, split it and spread butter, jam, or cream cheese. It works well for sandwiches, toasties and appetizers. Warm rolls are often paired with hot chocolate or coffee.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the roll in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage place it in the refrigerator (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Reheat in the oven before serving to restore a crisp crust.
